items.title: A00→A05: native QueryAbi errno and 21 strict HOSR verifier negatives
items.body:
## A00→A05: correct the experimental Asterinas HOS2 ioctl structural errno boundary

**Exact upstream A05 Draft source:** [PR #87](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/pull/87) HEAD `5fc3887dfc5833b61d11280eb1421bb7fd78648f`. Independent A00 branch `agents/A00-a05-queryabi-errno-contract`, three commits; changes **only two A05-owned files**: `kernel/asterinas/kernel/core/src/device/misc/hepta_control.rs` and `tests/kernel/control/queryabi_guest.c`. A05 original branch is untouched, no force push, no A00/main or protocol/golden modification.

### Concrete protocol defect in the original candidate

The project source of truth [docs/NATIVE_ABI.md §3](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/blob/main/docs/NATIVE_ABI.md) requires **unknown ioctl→ENOTTY**, **unknown protocol version/magic→EPROTONOSUPPORT**, **unknown opcode/recognized but unsupported→EOPNOTSUPP**, **malformed input→EINVAL**, **output below successful frame capacity→EMSGSIZE**, **usercopy faults→EFAULT**. A05's first real kernel QueryAbi `ioctl` implementation collapsed every A02 `decode_request_snapshot` error into `EINVAL`, labeled recognized disabled operations as `ENOTTY`, and rejected any bounded non-64-byte HOS2 request as unknown ioctl. That makes a client unable to distinguish a recoverable short output buffer or an unsupported operation from malformed input. This is a **real source-level ABI integration mismatch**, not a demonstrated guest exploit.

### Small, allocation-free fix

* Snapshot bounded known HOS2 requests up to `HEADER_LEN + 40 = 104` bytes with one kernel userspace copy. The exact shared A02 decoder remains authoritative; **no second wire codec, grants, CAS, retirement or resource state machine** are added.
* Map `wire::Error::InvalidMagic|UnknownVersion` to `EPROTONOSUPPORT`, `UnknownOpcode` and valid unsupported known operations to `EOPNOTSUPP`, and `InsufficientCapacity` to `EMSGSIZE`. Keep other structural errors as EINVAL, invalid user-space buffers as the kernel's native EFAULT, and unrelated ioctl commands ENOTTY.
* Add true Asterinas **guest-only negative tests** to `queryabi_guest.c`: unknown magic, unsupported major, unknown opcode, 111-byte QueryAbi response vs required 112, valid but disabled ReadUsage (128-byte output), valid ordered InstallBudget (96-byte request, 128-byte output), malformed header length, NULL transport and unknown ioctl. The InstallBudget negative intentionally uses canonical little-endian D sequence, zero high request ID, nonzero handle, 100ms period and legal cap, to ensure the error is due to unsupported operation rather than invalid encoding. Original positive per-open IDs/boot identity checks remain.

### Strict evidence and owner gate

All writes were made through GitHub with original blob preimage checks. **The new fixed-nightly Asterinas kernel and its guest C probe have NOT been compiled or executed on this exact A00 head** (the present local tool runtime lacks Rust/cargo/QEMU). C guest additions are source-level negatives, not claimed passing cases. The original A05 Draft #87 reports a completed full native build of its **older, unchanged code**, but no successful actual QueryAbi device guest execution; this PR does not inherit that result.

Keep **Draft** until A05 reviews this stacked two-file patch, checks exact-head `nightly-2026-07-21` build and `cc -std=c11 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -static` guest, and executes the full positive/negative probe in a disposable one-vCPU QEMU initramfs. Validate access from uid!=0, dup/fork/exec and abort/copyout EFAULT before any main integration. The ioctl number remains explicitly **experimental**, only QueryAbi advertises bit1, and a genuine trusted kernel CapSpace/device permission story is still required. Neither physical devices nor Hepta durable business effects were accessed.

### Independent exact Git-blob native C compilation (subsequent verification)

After publishing the corrected test guest, I fetched `tests/kernel/control/queryabi_guest.c` from the **earlier source HEAD** and reconstructed it in an isolated Linux x86_64 workspace. The local `git blob` SHA1, computed over `blob 4793\0 + file bytes`, is **`2cfdd3be52d7a79697ae4486eb97a4389858265e`**, **identical** to GitHub's committed source blob. Real command:

`cc -std=c11 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic -static a05-queryabi-guest-validation.c -o a05-queryabi-guest-validation`

**Exit 0, no warnings.** The result is an **ELF64 little-endian x86-64, statically linked** guest-compatible Linux executable, 759,048 bytes; local SHA256 `3e07153491b10684f4c87f830b6518a49e0befc9914a26796a556cede60ae8b3`. `readelf -h` confirms EM_X86_64, ELF64 and executable type. The binary has **not been executed on an Asterinas guest or production hardware**, and the patched kernel Rust was **not compiled** here; these negative ioctl assertions are authored and compilable but still await QEMU. Distinguish this verified guest ELF compilation from the separate Linux-host HOS2 ENOTTY smoke.

### Latest exact guest proof (supersedes the earlier 4,793-byte C source)

Further adversarial inspection found the disabled `InstallBudget` negative needed an explicit HOS2 **payload_len=32** field, in addition to its correct target, period, cap and ordered request ID. Without that field the decoder would rightly reject the malformed frame as EINVAL, so it would not test the actual EOPNOTSUPP branch. Commit `a9b529e0643695265b8bac561920032a6d12b91b` fixes this in the test source.

**New exact GitHub test blob:** `51b8bccc73bc36884084d67bd1141c6d4322d899`, 4,815 bytes. Local independent `git hash-object` matched that same SHA byte-for-byte. A new strict `cc -std=c11 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic -static` compilation on these **latest** bytes exited **0** without warnings; ELF is statically linked x86_64, size 759,048 bytes, SHA256 `c132e8dce31ecfb187b960dd09a37013963e3cf88e5607ec4ff973aa64768679`. The prior test blob and binary hashes are **superseded**; the patched kernel Rust and actual QEMU device exercise remain unexecuted and #88 remains Draft.

### Parallel A05 verifier consolidation — latest exact head

An independently owned A00 branch [PR #90](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/pull/90) hardened the **same** `queryabi_guest.c` HOSR verifier against nonzero minor/header-reserved/QueryAbi-payload-reserved bytes, and added a mandatory C host oracle. Rather than clobber its work, A00 constructed the exact combined tree from PR #90, overlaying only PR #88's kernel errno fix and a merged guest checker. A true **two-parent no-force merge** `97d1c5f4ea638863fb068cd7a3b44e93d31f6a3c` now preserves both PR #88 and PR #90's ancestry. Against the PR #90 branch the current merged diff is **only** two A05-owned files: `hepta_control.rs` and `queryabi_guest.c`. Do not independently merge conflicting pre-merge guest versions.

**Latest exact-source independent Linux validation:** Combined guest Git blob `ad9ce99f5214d441d6904028e5ef8b1de922a0f4` (4,955 bytes), matched exactly by `git hash-object` in the local host. `cc -std=c11 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic -static` successfully compiled that exact source into ELF64 x86_64, SHA256 `853f3d65f390316c0f91ea1e36534b58e720e591a183fdfc40d7fba7621407fe`, no warnings. PR #90's exact C host oracle blob `ea9e60c4e6e02d542fb4e9df9778a6a671a3943b` also matches local bytes; **compiled and executed** on Linux with exit 0, reporting **1 valid HOSR frame plus 21 invalid mutations rejected**. The original guest positive/negative ioctl assertions were compiled but **not** run in this host-model test.

The previous C guest blob `51b8b...` and binary SHA256 `c132e8...` refer to the *pre-consolidation* version and are superseded by the exact hashes above. None of this qualifies the **new Asterinas kernel build or QEMU ioctl behavior on the combined tree**, so PR #88 stays **Draft** until A05 owner review and fixed nightly kernel/QEMU positive+negative tests.

Base: actual main `7d5121a41090dc74521de8a6a14d923d9dfc34db`. Only A05-owned `tests/kernel/control/**` files change (two existing host files and one test-only C fault shim). **Reproduced bug:** merged A05 [PR #42](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/pull/42) treats any `ioctl` failure as exit 77.
